chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, and others, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, all from Musa ibn Umra, from Gassan al-Basri, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from one of our companions, from Ibrahim ibn Uqba, from Muawiya ibn Wahb who said:

I sought permission to enter upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so it was said to me, 'Enter'. So I entered and found him in his prayer mat in his house. So I sat until he finished his prayer, and I heard him as he was conversing with his Lord, saying: 'O He who distinguished us with honor, and distinguished us with the successorship, and promised us intercession, and gave us knowledge of what has passed and what remains, and made the hearts of people incline towards us.'

Forgive me and my brothers, and the visitors of the grave of Abu Abdillah al-Husayn (peace be upon him), who spent their wealth and sent their bodies, desiring our goodness and hoping for what is with You regarding maintaining ties with us, and bringing joy to Your Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and answering our command, and bringing rage to our enemy, intending thereby Your pleasure.

So suffice them from us with contentment, and protect them by night and day, and compensate for their families and children who were left behind with the best compensation, and accompany them, and suffice them from the evil of every stubborn tyrant, and every weak or strong of Your creation, and the evil of the devils of humans and jinn, and give them the best of what they hoped for from You in their exile from their homelands, and what they preferred us with over their sons, families, and relatives.

O Allah, our enemies criticized them for their departure, but that did not prevent them from traveling to us, and opposing those who opposed us. So have mercy on those faces which the sun has changed, and have mercy on those cheeks which rolled upon the grave of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and have mercy on those eyes from which tears flowed out of mercy for us, and have mercy on those hearts which were anxious and burned for us, and have mercy on the cry which was for us. O Allah, I entrust to You those souls and those bodies until we meet them at the Pond on the Day of Thirst.

So he remained as he was in prostration, supplicating with this supplication. So when he finished, I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, if this which I heard from you was for one who does not know Allah, I would think that the Fire would not consume anything from him. By Allah, I wished that I had visited him and had not performed Hajj.' So he said to me, 'How close you are to him, so what is preventing you from going to him?'

Then he said, 'O Muawiya, why do you leave that?' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, I did not know that the matter reached all of this.' He said, 'O Muawiya, those who supplicate for his visitors in the sky are more than those who supplicate for them on the earth.'

key_terms.الْحَوْض: The Pond (of the Prophet in the afterlife)
key_terms.الْغُرْبَة: Exile or being strangers away from home

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of visiting the grave of Imam al-Husayn according to Imam al-Sadiq's supplication?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the intercessory power of the Imams, specifically Imam al-Sadiq’s (as) supplication for those who sacrifice wealth and health to visit Imam al-Husayn (as). It underscores the Shia concept of *Ziyarah* as a means of spiritual proximity and divine favor, culminating in the profound insight that angels in the heavens supplicate for visitors more abundantly than humans on earth, reinforcing the cosmic significance of this devotional act.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, and someone else, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad and Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, altogether from Musa Bin Umra, from Gassan Al basry, from Muawiya Bin Wahab, and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from one of our companions, from Ibrahim Bin Uqba, from Muawiya Bin Wahab who said,

‘I sought permission to see Abu Abdullahasws, so it was said to me, ‘Enter’. So I went in and found himasws to be upon hisasws Prayer mat in hisasws room. So, I sat down until heasws had completed hisasws Salaat. Then I heard himasws, and heasws was whispering to hisasws Lordazwj, and saying: ‘O the Oneazwj Who Specialised usasws with the Prestige, and Specialised usasws with the successor-ship, and Promised usasws (the right of) intercession, and Granted usasws knowledge what is past and what remains, Made the hearts of the people to incline towards usasws.

(The prayer for a believer) Forgive me, and my brethren, and the visitors of the grave of Abu Abdullah Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> who spent their wealth, and drove their bodies wishing to be good to us<sup>asws</sup>, and hoping for what is in Your<sup>azwj</sup> Presence regarding maintaining relationships with us<sup>asws</sup> and the cheerfulness entering upon Your<sup>azwj</sup> Prophet<sup>saww</sup>, and their answering to our<sup>asws</sup> orders, and the rage which they entered upon our<sup>asws</sup> enemies intending by that Your<sup>azwj</sup> Pleasure.

Therefore, suffice them from us<sup>asws</sup> with the contentment and Care for them by the night and the day, and Look after their families and their children whom they have left behind, with the best care; and Accompany them and Suffice them from the evil of every stubborn tyrant, from every weak ones of Your<sup>azwj</sup> creatures and the strong ones, and evil of the devils, and the human beings, and the jinn, and Give them the best of what is to be Granted from You<sup>azwj</sup> regarding their being strangers away from their homelands, and what they preferred us<sup>asws</sup> with upon their own sons, and their families, and their relatives.

O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Our<sup>asws</sup> enemies faulted them for their going towards (our<sup>asws</sup> shrines), but that did not prevent them from the travelling to us<sup>asws</sup>, and they opposed (all of) those who had opposed us<sup>asws</sup>. So be Merciful to those faces whom the sun has changed, and be Merciful to those cheeks which kissed upon the grave of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, and be Merciful to those eyes which flowed its tears in sympathy with us<sup>asws</sup>, and be Merciful to those hearts which mourned and burnt for us<sup>asws</sup>, and be Merciful to the screams which were for us<sup>asws</sup>. O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! I hereby entrust to You<sup>azwj</sup> those selves, and those bodies until we<sup>asws</sup> fulfil (our<sup>asws</sup> Promises to them) at the Fountain on the day of the thirst’.

So heasws did not cease to be in Prostration supplicating with this supplication. So when heasws finished, I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for youasws! If this, which I heard from youasws was for the one who does not recognise Allahazwj, I think that the Fire would not consume anything from him. By Allahazwj! I wish that I had performed hisasws Ziyarah and had not performed Hajj’. So heasws said to me: ‘How close heasws is to you. So what is that which prevents you from going to himasws?’

Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Muawiya! Why did you leave that?’ I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! I did not know that the matter had reach all of this (significance)’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Muawiya! The ones who supplicate for his<sup>asws</sup> visitors in the sky are more than the ones who supplicate for them in the earth’.
en.sarwar: 11. Muhammad ibn Yahya and others have narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn all from Musa ibn ‘Umar from Ghassan al-Basriy from Mu‘awiyah ibn Wahab Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from certain individuals of our people from Ibrahim ibn ‘Uqbah from Mu‘awiyah ibn Wahab who has said the following:

“I once asked permission to see abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and permission was granted. I was told to come in. When I went inside, I found him in his place for salat (prayer) in his house. I then sat down until he completed his salat (prayer). I then heard him secretly speaking to his Lord. ‘O the One who has granted us honor in a special way, O the one who has granted us exclusive executorships of the will of the messengers and has promised us intercession, granted us the knowledge of the past and future and has made the hearts of people to incline toward us,

forgive me and my brothers (in belief). (O Lord, forgive) the visitors of the grave of abu ‘Abd Allah, al-Husayn, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, who spend their wealth. Those who ready their bodies due to their interest in doing good to us and because of their hope in what is with You of compensation for keeping good relations with us and because of the happiness they bring to the heart of Your prophet. I appeal before Allah to grant salawat (favors and compensation to Your Holy prophet and his family worthy of his services to Your cause) and forgive them because of their yielding to our commands and because of the anger due to their visit they cause to our enemies. In doing so, they only want to find that You are happy with them.

So compensate them on our behalf by being happy with them, and support them in the night and day. Be their deputy in their families and children whom they have left behind, as best deputy. Accompany them and protect them against the evil of every hostile tyrant, weak ones of Your creatures or strong ones, and against the evil of the devils of humankind and al-Jinn. Grant them the best, which they are to receive from You in their condition of being in strange places away from their homes and because of the preference they have given to us over their own children, families and relatives.

O Allah, our enemies mock at them for their visiting us, but this does not prevent them from setting on their journey toward us and from opposing those who oppose us. So be kind to the faces, which the heat of sun has changed. Be kind to the side of those faces, which are turned from side to side over the grave of abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam. Be kind to those eyes, which have shed tears in sympathy with us. Be kind to the hearts, which mourned and felt pain for us. Be kind to the wailing cries for us. O Allah, I entrust those souls and bodies with You until the time we meet, and compensate them at the pond (in paradise) on the dehydrating day.’

He (the Imam) continued with such prayers in a prostrating position. When he completed, I said, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, if what I heard from you were for even those who do not know Allah, I think, hellfire would not touch them. I by Allah, wished to have visited the grave of al-Husayn, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, instead of performing al-Hajj.’ He (the Imam) said to me, ‘He is much closer to you. What then prevents you from visiting him?’

He (the Imam) then said, ‘O Mu‘awiyah, why do you neglect such visitations?’ I said, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, I did not know the matter is of all such great degrees of significance.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘O Mu‘awiyah, the number of those who pray for the visitors of al- Husayn, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, in the heavens is much greater than those who pray for them on earth.’”
